result.summary: The image shows an urban intersection with brick residential or mixed-use buildings and sidewalks on both sides. While traffic signals are present, the crosswalk markings are significantly faded, and there is a lack of visible pedestrian-specific infrastructure like signals or curb ramps.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The painted crosswalk lines are heavily worn, making the pedestrian crossing less visible to approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signals are visible at this signalized intersection, which can lead to confusion about when it is safe to cross.

hazards.name: Missing Curb Ramps
hazards.description: No ADA-compliant curb ramps are visible at the crossing points, creating a significant barrier for people with mobility aids.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk using high-visibility continental or ladder markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install sloped curb ramps with detectable warning surfaces at all crossing points.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized urban intersection with high-visibility continental crosswalks and wide sidewalks in a mixed-use area. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, the crossing distance is relatively long for a one-way street, and parked vehicles near the corner may limit visibility.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb near the intersection can obscure pedestrians, especially children, from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the right curb, upstream of the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Degraded pavement surface
hazards.description: Cracking and uneven pavement in the roadway near the crosswalk could present a minor tripping hazard or affect vehicle braking.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Constructing curb extensions would shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and improve visibility by moving pedestrians past the line of parked cars before they enter the travel lane.

interventions.description: Removing parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sightlines between motorists and pedestrians.
